newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Somali drought causes starvation, lion attacks.
newsitem.headline: Somali drought causes starvation, lion attacks.

text.p: Drought has caused 11 deaths from starvation in the Somali capital in the last three weeks and led to lion attacks on herdsmen in an outlying district, a faction official and witnesses said on Wednesday.
The official with the faction headed by Hassan Ali Osman Atto said the 11, most of them displaced people, had died in southern Mogadishu because they could not find enough to eat.

He appealed for international aid and said the security of aid agencies would be guaranteed at an airstrip under the control of the Atto faction. Its appeal and warning of famine followed similar statements by Mogadishu's other factions.
Witnesses meanwhile said seven lions attacked herdsmen and cattle at a reservoir in Wanlewein district, 90 km (55 miles) south of the capital, wounding three men and killing five cows.
Villagers, who shot one lion dead, said they believed the lions had been forced into inhabited areas by the drought.
The U.N. World Food Programme and Food and Agriculture Organisation forecast in December the secondary crop in southern regions of maize and sorghum would be 45 percent less than average.
They said livestock prices in the southwest had fallen and cereal prices had increased and if the secondary rainy season failed herders who had lost livestock would require food aid.

A shortage of water for pastoralists in much of barren Somalia is an annual problem, forcing them to move livestock to other areas during the dry season. Some 300,000 people were killed by famine fuelled by civil war in Somalia in 1992.
